quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night instead of during the day, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Keep more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam when possible.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, ride slower and leave more space between you and other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: What is NOT needed for an eye or face shield to work well?

options.text: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle horn?

options.text: Other people usually cannot hear it.
It can quickly get someone's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn is useful for getting someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely on your horn alone to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: What can help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make sure other drivers can see you. Use turn signals, your brake light, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and to the sides of the road. Always be prepared to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: Which clothing item gives a motorcyclist good protection?

options.text: A jacket that leaves arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Footwear should have low heels that will not catch on foot pegs or the road. Leather or durable gloves protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the usual sign of tire failure.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials all the time helps other drivers see you better.

questions.question: What is true about a shatter-resistant face shield?

options.text: It can protect your face during a crash.
It should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect your face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only, not the rest of your face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces, such as wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This applies in all road conditions.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will likely correct itself.
Close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly. Slowly close the throttle to reduce speed. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible and check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: If you are riding and your motorcycle starts to handle differently, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you notice different handling, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Alternate between your headlight's low and high beam settings.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colored clothing when riding. This helps other drivers see you, even in daylight.

questions.question: You should do all of the following to reduce your chances of crashing, except:

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Show your intentions by using your turn signals and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope the other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope the other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to other drivers, signal your intentions, and keep space around you. Look for hazards and be ready to react to anything.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Limiting the distance ridden in one day

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not use artificial stimulants. They can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If a person drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks will likely remain in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining, subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. Example: Seven drinks in three hours, then three more hours pass. Seven minus six hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far enough back on the seat that you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle rather than support your body. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, the riders should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When a group of motorcyclists passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. Wait until one rider has finished passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead of you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the car. This place you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate any motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is located on the right handlebar grip. Learn the locations of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should the motorcycle and rider do?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.
